items.title: Line Graph · International Students in Three Countries
items.summary: Describe and compare trends over 20 years; practise the overview and trend vocabulary.

items.title: Bar Chart · Household Spending 1990 vs 2020
items.summary: Compare proportions across categories and two years; practise grouping data.

items.title: Pie Charts · Electricity Sources 2000 vs 2020
items.summary: Compare two pie charts; describe a shift from coal to gas and renewables.

items.title: Table · Public Transport in Five Cities
items.summary: Select key features from a table with three variables; compare by column.

items.title: Process · Recycling Plastic Bottles
items.summary: Describe a man-made process using the passive voice and sequencers.

items.title: Process · Rainwater Harvesting System
items.summary: Describe a system with a branching end-point; mix active and passive verbs.

items.title: Maps · Westbury Town Centre Then and Now
items.summary: Compare two maps using present perfect passive and location language.

items.title: Mixed Charts · Tourism Arrivals and Purpose of Visit
items.summary: Combine a line graph and bar chart; describe a peak, a collapse and a recovery.

items.title: Bar Chart · Time Online by Age Group
items.summary: Describe absolute vs proportional change across five age groups.

items.title: Maps · Planned Campus Redevelopment
items.summary: Describe planned changes using future passive forms.

items.title: Line Graph · House Prices in Three Cities
items.summary: Describe diverging trends, a peak and a dip; practise approximation language.

items.title: Process · Life Cycle of a Butterfly
items.summary: Describe a natural cycle using active verbs and stage vocabulary.

items.title: Table · Waste Management in Four Countries
items.summary: Compare percentages across categories and countries; find the key contrasts.

items.title: Bar Chart · Regular Exercise by Age and Gender
items.summary: Compare two groups across five categories; describe a reversal.

items.title: Line Graph · Renewable Electricity in Four Countries
items.summary: Describe four lines with different starting points and growth rates.

items.title: Pie Chart + Table · Student Budgets
items.summary: Combine a pie chart and a table; link the two sources in the overview.

items.title: Process · How Chocolate Is Made
items.summary: A process with natural and man-made stages; mix active and passive.

items.title: Maps · A Fishing Village Becomes a Resort
items.summary: Describe transformation from a fishing village to a tourist resort.

items.title: Opinion · Should University Be Free for All?
items.summary: Agree/disagree essay with a partial position and a proposed alternative.

items.title: Discussion · Competition or Cooperation at School?

items.title: Advantages & Disadvantages · Working from Home

items.title: Causes & Solutions · Traffic Congestion
items.summary: Identify causes and match each with a specific solution.

items.title: Two-part Question · Why Are People Moving to Cities?
items.summary: Answer a 'why' question and give a positive/negative verdict.

items.title: Positive or Negative? · More People Living Alone
items.summary: Evaluate a social trend for individuals and for society.

items.title: Opinion · Compulsory Community Service at School
items.summary: Strongly agree essay with a counter-argument and rebuttal paragraph.

items.title: Discussion · Public Money for the Arts?
items.summary: Discuss arts funding vs public services and challenge the either/or premise.

items.title: Opinion · Will AI Replace Teachers?
items.summary: Nuanced disagree essay on technology in education.

items.title: Advantages Outweigh? · International Tourism
items.summary: Weigh advantages against disadvantages and reach a clear verdict.

items.title: Discussion · Who Should Protect the Environment?

items.title: Causes & Solutions · Young People Reading Less
items.summary: Explain a social trend and propose matching, practical solutions.

items.title: Opinion · Should Rich Countries Help Poorer Nations?

items.title: Two-part Question · Celebrities as Role Models
items.summary: Explain celebrity influence and judge whether it is positive or negative.

items.title: Opinion · Ban Private Cars from City Centres?

items.title: Discussion · Online vs Classroom Learning

items.title: Advantages & Disadvantages · An Ageing Population

items.title: Causes & Solutions · Youth Unemployment

items.title: Two-part Question · The Shift to Online Shopping

items.title: Opinion · Is Space Exploration Worth the Money?
items.summary: Disagree essay defending space spending with concrete benefits.

items.title: Opinion · Should Students Study Only Useful Subjects?
items.summary: Disagree essay on the value of non-vocational degrees.

items.title: Discussion · Longer Hours or Better Balance?
items.summary: Discuss whether long working hours increase success.

items.title: Advantages Outweigh? · Personal DNA Testing
items.summary: Weigh the benefits and risks of home genetic tests.

items.title: Causes & Solutions · Noise in Cities
items.summary: Explain the causes and effects of urban noise and propose solutions.

items.title: Two-part Question · Why Fewer People Volunteer

items.title: Positive or Negative? · Going Cashless
items.summary: Evaluate the move from cash to digital payments.

items.title: Part 1 · Work or Study
items.summary: 5 Part 1 questions on work or study with natural model answers.
questions: Do you work or are you a student?
Why did you choose that job / subject?
What do you like most about it?
Is there anything you dislike about it?
Would you like to change your job in the future?

questions: Where is your hometown?
What do you like about your hometown?
Has your hometown changed much in recent years?

items.title: Part 2 & 3 · A Person Who Influenced You
items.summary: Describe a person who has had an important influence on your life.

bullets: how long you have known them
and explain why they have influenced you so much

part3_questions: Who usually has more influence on children — parents or teachers?
Do you think celebrities are good role models for young people?

items.title: Part 2 & 3 · A Place You Want to Revisit

cue_card.task: Describe a place you have visited that you would like to go back to.
bullets: and explain why you would like to go back

part3_questions: Why do some people prefer to visit the same place again and again?

Should the number of tourists visiting some places be limited?

part3_questions: What skills do you think children should learn at school apart from academic subjects?

items.title: Part 2 & 3 · A Memorable Journey
items.summary: Describe a memorable journey you have made.

cue_card.task: Describe a memorable journey you have made.

part3_questions: Do you think people will travel more or less in the future?

items.title: Part 2 & 3 · A Time You Helped Someone
items.summary: Describe a time when you helped someone.

cue_card.task: Describe a time when you helped someone.

part3_questions: Why do some people not help others?

cue_card.task: Describe a piece of technology (not a phone) that you use often.

part3_questions: How has technology changed the way people work?

items.title: Articles: a, an, the, Ø

items.title: Subject–Verb Agreement
items.summary: Make verbs agree with their real subject, even in long noun phrases.

items.title: Relative Clauses & Complex Sentences
items.summary: Combine ideas with who/which/that/where/whose to raise your Grammatical Range score.

items.title: Conditionals for Arguments

items.title: The Passive Voice
items.summary: Essential for process diagrams, maps and formal academic style.

items.title: Tenses for Task 1 and Task 2

items.title: Common Errors: Countable Nouns, Prepositions, Word Forms
items.summary: Fix the small errors that pull Band 6 scripts down.

items.title: Hedging & Modal Verbs
items.summary: Soften claims like an academic writer: may, might, could, tend to, it is likely that.

items.title: Gerunds & Infinitives
items.summary: Choose -ing or to + verb after common verbs, adjectives and prepositions.

items.title: Sentence Boundaries & Punctuation
items.summary: Avoid comma splices and fragments; use commas, semicolons and colons correctly.

items.title: Nominalisation & Noun Phrases
items.summary: Turn verbs and adjectives into nouns to write in a concise, academic style.

items.title: Quantifiers: much, many, few, little, a number of

items.title: Prepositions for Data & Time
items.summary: Use by, of, at, to, from, between correctly when describing numbers and trends.

items.title: Emphasis: Cleft Sentences & Inversion
items.summary: Add emphasis and variety with 'What … is', 'It is … that' and negative inversion.

items.title: Future Forms & Predictions
items.summary: Express predictions, plans and probability about the future accurately.
